newsitem.title: USA: High spending, demand unlikely to continue -- Moskow.
newsitem.headline: High spending, demand unlikely to continue -- Moskow.

text.p: High levels of U.S. spending and demand seen in the first quarter are not likely to persist for the rest of the year, Chicago Federal Reserve Bank President Michael Moskow said on Thursday.
"As we look forward through the year, I would not expect that the level of demand and spending in the economy would continue at this rate," Moskow said at a news briefing.
Moskow said milder weather may have played a role in the strong Q1 GDP. "Sometimes spending and demand tends to be moved from one quarter to another depending on factors like the weather," he said.
The economy grew 5.6 percent on an annual basis in the first quarter, while consumer spending rose at 6.4 percent, the government reported on Wednesday.
